newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Onfem to buy stake in magnet company.
newsitem.headline: Onfem to buy stake in magnet company.

text.p: Onfem Holdings said on Monday it has agreed to buy a 62 percent stake in United States-based MQ Holdings in a bid to enter into the magnetic materials industry.

"Through this acquisition, Onfem will successfully enter into a high-tech industry engaged in the development, manufacturing and distribution of magnetic materials," said managing director Fang Dacheng at a news conference.

Onfem, which suspended trading in its shares in Hong Kong on Monday, would buy a 47 percent stake in MQ Holdings from China National Nonferrous Metals Import and Export Corporation (CNIEC) and 15 percent from San Huan New Materials and Hightech, Inc.

Onfem would make initial payments of HK$43.6 million (US$5.64 million) to CNIEC and HK$13.9 million (US$1.8 million) to San Huan, followed by final payments based on MQ's future consolidated profits, Fang said.
The purchase would give Onfem an indirect 37.2 percent stake in MQ Holdings's 60 percent-owned Magnequench International Inc which manufactures and markets neodymium magnetic materials.
Neodymium magnets are far more powerful than magnets made from hard ferrite and are used extensively in modern computers, electronic appliances and motor vehicles, amongst others.
